title: Tarte Tatin
ahead: Bake the apples in their caramel the day before.
notes: The baked apples keep 3 days in the fridge before the pastry goes on.
Best the day it is baked; the pastry softens after a few hours.

ingredients.name: round sheet of all-butter puff pastry

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160 °C conventional / 140 °C fan.
Put {sugar} in a 24 cm cast-iron or ovenproof pan over medium heat. Cook without stirring, swirling the pan now and then, until melted and deep amber.
Off the heat, stir in {butter} and {salt}. It will bubble up hard.
Stand {apples} on their edges in the caramel, packed tightly in circles, and pile the rest on top. They shrink a lot.
Bake on a middle rack until the apples have slumped.
Press the apples down with a spatula to close the gaps. Bake until deep amber, soft right through and sunk into one dense layer.
Cool, cover and refrigerate overnight, so the apples set.
Heat the oven to 200 °C conventional / 180 °C fan.
Lay {pastry} over the pan and trim it 2 cm wider than the apples. Tuck the edge down inside the pan, then prick all over with a fork.
Bake until the pastry is puffed and deep golden.
Rest in the pan, so the caramel stops bubbling.
Shake the pan until the tart slides freely, warming it over medium heat if it sticks. Put a large plate on top and flip in one quick motion.
Put back any apple left in the pan. Serve warm, with {cream} on the table.
